verses.sanskrit:
युधिष्ठिर उवाच।
              कच्चित्पितामहेनासीच्छ्रुतं वा दृष्टमेव च । कच्चिन्मर्त्यो मृतो राजन् पुनरुज्जीवितोऽभवत् ॥१॥
verses.english: Bhishma said The next morning, king Janaka, O Bharata, accompanied by his minister and the whole household, came to Shuka, preceded by his priest.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              शृणु पार्थ यथावृत्तमितिहासं पुरातनम् । गृध्रजम्बुकसंवादं यो वृत्तो नैमिषे पुरा ॥२॥
verses.english: Bringing with him rich seats and various sorts of jewels and gems, and bearing the ingredients of the Arghya on his own head, the king approached the son of his reverend preceptor.

verses.sanskrit: कस्यचिद्ब्राह्मणस्यासीद्दुःखलब्धः सुतो मृतः । बाल एव विशालाक्षो बालग्रहनिपीडितः ॥३॥
verses.english: The king, taking with his own hands, from the hands of his priest, that seat adorned with many gems, covered with an excellent sheet, beautiful in all its parts and dearly costly, presented it with great respect to his preceptor's son Shuka.

verses.sanskrit: दुःखिताः केचिदादाय बालमप्राप्तयौवनम् । कुलसर्वस्वभूतं वै रुदन्तः शोकविह्वलाः ॥४॥
verses.english: After the son of Krishna had taken his seat on it, the king adored him according to prescribed rites. At first offering him water to wash his feet, he then presented him the Arghya and kine.

verses.sanskrit: बालं मृतं गृहीत्वाऽथ श्मशानाभिमुखाः स्थिताः । अङ्केनैव च संक्रम्य रुरुदुर्भृशदुःखिताः ॥५॥
verses.english: The ascetic accepted that worship offered with due rites and Mantras. That foremost of twice-born ones, having thus accepted the worship offered by the king, and taking the kine also that were presented to him, then saluted the king, gifted with great energy, he next enquired after the king's welfare and prosperity.

verses.sanskrit: शोचन्तस्तस्य पूर्वोक्तान् भाषितांश्चासकृत्पुनः । तं बालं भूतले क्षिप्य प्रतिगन्तुं न शक्नुयुः ॥६॥
verses.english: Indeed, O king, Shuka asked about the welfare of the king's followers and officers also. Receiving Shuka's permission, Janaka sat down with all his followers.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां रुदितशब्देन गृध्रोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत् । एकात्मजमिमं लोके त्यक्त्वा गच्छत मा चिरम् ॥७॥
verses.english: Having a high soul and possessed of high birth, the king with joined hands, sat down on the bare ground and enquired after the wellbeing and unabated prosperity of Vyasa's son. The king then asked his guest the object of his visit.

verses.sanskrit: इह पुंसां सहस्राणि स्त्रीसहस्राणि चैव ह । समानीतानि कालेन हित्वा वै यान्ति बान्धवाः ॥८॥
verses.english: Shuka said Blessed be you, my father told me that his client, the king of the Videhas, known all over the world by the name of Janaka, is well-versed in the Religion of Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: सम्पश्यत जगत्सर्वं सुखदुःखैरधिष्ठितम् । संयोगो विप्रयोगश्च पर्यायेणोपलभ्यते ॥९॥
verses.english: He ordered me to come to him forthwith, if I had any doubts to be solved in the Religion of either Action or Renunciation. He gave me to understand that the king of Mithila would remove all my doubts.

verses.sanskrit: गृहीत्वा ये च गच्छन्ति ये न यान्ति च तान् मृतान् । तेऽप्यायुषः प्रमाणेन स्वेन गच्छन्ति जन्तवः ॥१०॥
verses.english: I have, therefore, come come here at the command of my father, for the purpose of receiving instruction from you. You should, O foremost of all righteous persons, instruct me!

verses.sanskrit: अलं स्थित्वा श्मशानेऽस्मिन् गृध्रगोमायुसंकुले । कङ्कालबहुले रौद्रे सर्वप्राणिभयङ्करे ॥११॥
verses.english: What are the duties of a Brahmana, and what is the essence of those duties that have Liberation for their object. How, also, is Liberation to be acquired. Is it to be acquired by the help of Knowledge or by that Penances?

verses.sanskrit: न पुनर्जीवितः कश्चित्कालधर्ममुपागतः । प्रियो वा यदि वा द्वेष्यः प्राणिनां गतिरीदृशी ॥१२॥
verses.english: Janaka said Hear what the Duties are of a Brahmana from the time of his birth. After his investiture, O son, with the sacred thread, he should give his attention to the study of the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वेण खलु मर्तव्यं मर्त्यलोके प्रसूयता । कृतान्तविहिते मार्गे मृतं को जीवयिष्यति ॥१३॥
verses.english: By practising penances and dutifully serving his preceptor, and observing the duties of Brahmacharya, O powerful one, he should satisfy the debt be owes to the gods, and the Pitris, and renounce all malice.

verses.sanskrit: कर्मान्तविरते लोके अस्तं गच्छति भास्करे । गम्यतां स्वमधिष्ठानं सुतस्नेहं विसृज्य वै ॥१४॥
verses.english: Having read the Vedas with close attention, and controlled his senses, and having given his preceptor the tuition-fee, he should, with the order of his preceptor, return home.

verses.sanskrit: ततो गृध्रवचः श्रुत्वा प्राक्रोशन्तस्तदा नृप । बान्धवास्तेऽभ्यगच्छन्त पुत्रमुत्सृज्य भूतले ॥१५॥
verses.english: Coming back home, he should follow the domestic mode of life and marry a wife, confine himself to her, and live freeing himself from every sort of malice, and having established his domestic fire.

verses.sanskrit: विनिश्चित्याथ च तदा विक्रोशन्तस्ततस्ततः । मृतमित्येव गच्छन्तो निराशास्तस्य दर्शने ॥१६॥
verses.english: Living as a householder, he should procreate sons and grandsons. After that, he should retire to the forest, and continue to adore the same fires and entertain guests with cordial hospitality.

verses.sanskrit: निश्चितार्थाश्च ते सर्वे संत्यजन्तः स्वमात्मजम् । निराशा जीविते तस्य मार्गमावृत्य धिष्ठिताः ॥१७॥
verses.english: Living virtuously in the forest, he should, at last, establish his fire in his soul, and freed from all pairs of opposites, and renouncing all attachments, he should pass his days in the anchorite-mode of life, which is otherwise called the mode of Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: ध्वांक्षपक्षसवर्णस्तु विलान्निसृत्य जम्बुकः ।  गच्छमानान् स्म तानाह निघृणाः खलु मानुषाः ॥१८॥
verses.english: Shuka said If one acquires an understanding cleansed by study of the scriptures and true conceptions of all things, and if the heart succeeds in freeing itself permanently from the effects of all pairs of opposites, is it still necessary for such a person to follow one after another, the three modes of life called Brahmacharya, Garahastya, and Vanaprastha.

verses.sanskrit: आदित्योऽयं स्थितो मूढाः स्नेहं कुरुत मा भयम् । बहुरूपो मुहूर्तश्च जीवेदपि कदाचन ॥१९॥
verses.english: This is what I ask you. You should me. Indeed, O king, do tell me this according to the true meaning of the Vedas.

verses.sanskrit: यूयं भूमौ विनिक्षिप्य पुत्रस्नेहविनाकृताः । श्मशाने सुतमुत्सृज्य कस्माद्गच्छत निर्घृणाः ॥२०॥
verses.english: Janaka said It is impossible to aquire Liberation without the help of an understanding purified by the study of the scriptures and without that true conception of all things which is known by the name of Vijnana, again, without that cleansed understanding, one cannot get a Preceptor.

verses.sanskrit: न वोऽस्त्यस्मिन्सुते स्नेहो बाले मधुरभाषिणि । यस्य भाषितमात्रेण प्रसादमधिगच्छत ॥२१॥
verses.english: The Preceptor is the helmsman, and Knowledge is the Boat. After having got that Boat, one becomes successful. Indeed, having crossed the Ocean, one may renounce both.

verses.sanskrit: ते पश्यत सुतस्नेहो यादृशः पशुपक्षिणाम् । न तेषां धारयित्वा तान् कश्चिदस्ति फलागमः ॥२२॥
verses.english: For preventing the destruction of all the worlds, and for preventing the destruction of deeds, the duties belonging to the four modes of life were practised by the wise of old.

verses.sanskrit: चतुष्पात्पक्षिकीटानां प्राणिनां स्नेहसङ्गिनाम् । परलोकगतिस्थानां मुनियज्ञक्रियामिव ॥२३॥
verses.english: By renouncing acts, good and bad, according to this order of acts, one succeeds, in course of many births, in acquiring Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: तेषां पुत्राभिरामाणामिहलोके परत्र च । न गुणो दृश्यते कश्चित्प्रजाः संधारयन्ति च ॥२४॥
verses.english: That man who, through penances, practised in many births, succeeds in acquiring purified mind and understanding, and soul, certainly becomes able to acquire Liberation in even the very first mode.

verses.sanskrit: अपश्यतां प्रियान्पुत्रान् तेषां शोको न तिष्ठति । न च पुष्णन्ति संवृद्धास्ते मातापितरौ क्वचित् ॥२५॥
verses.english: When, having acquired cleansed understanding, Liberation becomes his, and on account thereof be becomes possessed of knowledge of all visible things, what desirable object is there to attain by following the three other modes of life? a

verses.sanskrit: मानुषाणां कुतः स्नेहो येषां शोको भविष्यति । इमं कुलकरं पुत्रं त्यक्त्वा क्व न गमिष्यथ ॥२६॥
verses.english: One should always renounce faults produced by the qualities of Rajas and Tamas. Following the path of Sattva, one should see Self by Self.

verses.sanskrit: चिरं मञ्चत बाष्पं च चिरं स्नेहेन पश्यत । एवंविधानि हीष्टानि दुस्त्यजानि विशेषतः ॥२७॥
verses.english: Seeing one's Self in all creatures and all creatures in one's self, one should live like acquatic animals living in water without being drenched by it.

verses.sanskrit: क्षीणस्याभियुक्तस्य श्मशानाभिमुखस्य च । बान्धवा यत्र तिष्ठन्ति तत्रान्यो नाधितिष्ठति ॥२८॥
verses.english: He who succeeds in getting over all pairs of opposites and resisting their influence, succeeds in renouncing all attachments, and acquires infinite happiness in the next world, going there like a bird soaring into the sky from below.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वस्य दयिताः प्राणाः सर्वः स्नेहं च विन्दति । तिर्यग्योनिष्वपि सतां स्नेहं पश्यत यादृशम् ॥२९॥
verses.english: Regarding it, there is a saying sung of old by king Yayati, and remembered, O sire, by all persons conversant with the Scriptures dealing with Liberation.

verses.sanskrit: त्यक्त्वा कथं गच्छथेमं पद्मलोलायताक्षिकम् । यथा नवोद्वाहकृतं स्नानमाल्यविभूषितम् ॥३०॥
verses.english: The effulgent ray exists in one's Soul and not any where else. It exists equally in all creatures. One can see it himself if his heart be given to Yoga.

verses.sanskrit: जम्बुकस्य वचः श्रुत्वा कृपणं परिदेवतः । न्यवर्तन्त तदा सर्वे शवार्थं ते स्म मानुषाः ॥३१॥
verses.english: When a person lives in such a way that another is not filled with fear on seeing him, and when a person is not himself filled with fear on seeing others, when a person ceases to cherish desire and malice, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: गृध्र उवाच । अहो वत नृशंसेन जम्बुकेनाल्पमेधसा । क्षुद्रेणोक्ता हीनसत्त्वा मानुषाः किं निवर्तथ ॥३२॥
पञ्चेन्द्रियपरित्यक्तं शुष्कं काष्ठत्वमागतम् । कस्माच्छोवथ तिष्ठन्तमात्मानं किं न शोचथ ॥३३॥
verses.english: By controlling the mind and the soul, by renouncing malice that stupefies the mind, and by throwing off desire and stupefaction, one is said to attain to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: तपः कुरुत वै तीव्रं मुच्यध्वं येन किल्बिषात् । तपसा लभ्यते सर्वं विलापः किं करिष्यति ॥३४॥
verses.english: When a person assumes an equality of attitude about all objects of hearing and vision, as also about all living creatures, and gets over all pairs of opposites, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: अनिष्टानि च भाग्यानि जातानि सह मूर्तिना । येन गच्छति बालोऽयं दत्त्वा शोकमनन्तकम् ॥३५॥
verses.english: When a person regards impartially praise and dispraise, gold and iron, happiness and misery, heat and cold, good and evil, the agreeable and the disagreeable, life and death, he is then said to attain to Brahma.

verses.sanskrit: धनं, गावः, सुवर्णं च मणिरत्नमथापि च । अपत्यं च तपोमूलं तपोयोगाच्च लभ्यते ॥३६॥
verses.english: One following the duties of the mendicant order should restrain his senses and the mind like a tortoise withdrawing its outstretched limbs.

verses.sanskrit: यथाकृता च भूतेषु प्राप्यते सुखदुःखिता । गृहीत्वा जायते जन्तुर्दुःखानि च सुखानि च ॥३७॥
verses.english: As a house covered with darkness, is capable of being seen with the help of a lighted lamp, similarly can the soul be seen with the help of the lamp of the understanding.

verses.sanskrit: न कर्मणा पितुः पुत्रः पिता वा पुत्रकर्मणा । मार्गेणान्येन गच्छन्ति बद्धाः सुकृतदुष्कृतैः ॥३८॥
verses.english: O foremost of intelligent persons, I see that all this knowledge that I am imparting to you, lives in you. Whatever else should be known by one desirous of learning the Religion of Liberation, is already known to you.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मं चरत यत्नेन न चाधर्मे मनः कृथाः । वर्तध्वं च यथाकालं दैवतेषु द्विजेषु च ॥३९॥
verses.english: O regenerate Rishi, I am convinced that through the mercy of your preceptor and through the instructions you have received, you have already transcended all objects of the senses.

verses.sanskrit: शोकं त्यजत दैन्यं च सुतस्नेहान्निवर्तत । त्यज्यतामयमाकाशे ततः शीघ्रं निवर्तत ॥४०॥
verses.english: O great ascetic, through the grace of your father, I have acquired omniscience, and hence I have succeeded in knowing you.

verses.sanskrit: यत्करोति शुभं कर्म तथा कर्म सुदारुणम् । तत्कर्तैव समश्नाति बान्धवानां किमत्र ह ॥४१॥
verses.english: Your knowledge is much greater than what you think it to be. Your perceptions also that result from intuition, are much greater than what you think them to be. Your power also is much greater than you are conscious of.

verses.sanskrit: इह त्यक्त्वा न तिष्ठन्ति बान्धवा बान्धवं प्रियम् । स्नेहमुत्सृज्य गच्छन्ति बाष्पपूर्णाविलेक्षणाः ॥४२॥
verses.english: Whether in consequence of your tender age, or of the doubts you have not been able to remove, or of the fear that is due to be unattainment of Liberation, you are conscious of that Knowledge due to Intuition, although it has originated in your mind.

verses.sanskrit: प्राज्ञो वा यदि वा मूर्खः सधनो निर्धनोऽपि वा । सर्वः कालवशं याति शुभाशुभसमन्वितः ॥४३॥
verses.english: After one's doubts have been removed by persons like us, one succeeds in opening the knots of one's heart, and, then, by a righteous endeavour, acquires, and becomes conscious of, that Knowledge. not one

verses.sanskrit: किं करिष्यथ शोचित्वा मृतं किमनुशोचथ । सर्वस्य हि प्रभुः कालो धर्मतः समदर्शनः ॥४४॥
verses.english: As regards yourself, you are one that has already acquired knowledge. Your intelligence is steady and tranquil. You are free from covetousness. For all that, O Brahmana, one never succeed, without endeavour in attaining to Brahma, which is the highest object of acquisition.

verses.sanskrit: यौवनस्थांश्च बालांश्च वृद्धान् गर्भगतानपि । सर्वानाविशते मृत्युरेवंभूतमिदं जगत् ॥४५॥
verses.english: You see no difference between happiness and misery. You are not covetous. You have no desire for dancing and song. You have no attachments.

verses.sanskrit: जम्बुक उवाच । अहो मन्दीकृतः स्नेहो गृध्रेणेहाल्पबुद्धिना । पुत्रस्नेहाभिभूतानां युष्माकं शोचतां भृशम् ॥४६॥
verses.english: You have no attachment to friends. You have no fear in things which fill with fear. O blessed one, I see that you consider equally a lump of gold and a clod of Earth.

verses.sanskrit: समैः सम्यक्प्रयुक्तैश्च वचनैः प्रत्ययोत्तरैः । यद्गच्छति जनश्चायं स्नेहमुत्सृज्य दुस्त्यजम् ॥४७॥
verses.english: Myself and other persons endued with wisdom, see you established in the highest and indestructible path of peace.

verses.sanskrit: अहो पुत्रवियोगेन मृतशून्योपसेवनात् । क्रोशतां सुभृशं दुःखं विवत्सानां गवामिव ॥४८॥
verses.english: O Brahmana, you discharge the duties of Brahmana and enjoy the fruit which should be his, and which is at one with the essence of the object represented by Liberation. What else have you to enquire of me?

verses.sanskrit: अद्य शोकं विजानामि मानुषाणां महीतले । स्नेहं हि कारणं कृत्वा ममाप्यश्रूण्यथापतन् ॥४९॥
verses.english: To-day, however, I perceive the extent of grief of human beings on earth. Seeing their great affection I had shed tears myself.

verses.sanskrit: यत्नो हि सततं कार्यस्ततो दैवेन सिद्ध्यति । दैवं पुरुषकारश्च कृतान्तेनोपपद्यते ॥५०॥
verses.english: One should always exert. From it and through destiny one succeeds. Exertion and destiny, joining together, yield fruits.

verses.sanskrit: अनिर्वेदः सदा कार्यो निर्वेदाद्धि कुतः सुखम् । प्रयत्नात्प्राप्यते ह्यर्थः कस्माद्गच्छथ निर्दयम् ॥५१॥
verses.english: One should always exert hopefully. How can happiness be secured from despondency? Objects of desire may be acquired by resolution. Why then do you return so heartlessly?

verses.sanskrit: आत्ममांसोपवृत्तं च शरीरार्धमयीं तनुम् । पितॄणां वंशकर्तारं वने त्यक्त्वा क्व यास्यथ ॥५२॥
verses.english: Where do you go, leaving in the forest this your own begotten son, this perpetuator of the race of his father.

verses.sanskrit: अथवाऽस्तंगते सूर्ये संध्याकाल उपस्थिते । ततो नेष्यथ वा पुत्रमिहस्था वा भविष्यथ ॥५३॥
verses.english: Stay here till the sun sets and the evening comes. You may then take away this boy with yourselves or remain here with him.

verses.sanskrit: गृध्र उवाच । अद्य वर्षसहस्रं मे साग्रं जातस्य मानुषाः । न च पश्यमि जीवन्तं मृतं स्त्रीपुंनपुंसकम् ॥५४॥
verses.english: I am, Ye men, thousand years old this day, but I have never seen a dead creature, male or female or eunuch, revive after death.

verses.sanskrit: मृता गर्भेषु जायन्ते जातमात्रा म्रियन्ति च । चङ्क्रमन्तो म्रियन्ते च यौवनस्थास्तथा परे ॥५५॥
verses.english: Some die in the womb; some die soon after birth; some die while crawling; some die in youth; and some in old age.

verses.sanskrit: अनित्यानीह भाग्यानि चतुष्पात्पक्षिणामपि । जङ्गमानां नगानां वाप्यायुरग्रेऽवतिष्ठते ॥५६॥
verses.english: The fortunes of all creatures, including beasts and birds, are fickle. The extent of life of all mobile and immobile creatures is fixed beforehand.

verses.sanskrit: इष्टदारवियुक्ताश्च पुत्रशोकान्वितास्तथा । दह्यमानाः स्म शोकेन गृहं गच्छन्ति नित्यशः ॥५७॥
verses.english: Shorn of wives and dear ones and filled with sorrow for children, men leave this spot every day with aggrieved hearts for returning home.

verses.sanskrit: अनिष्टानां सहस्राणि तथेष्टानां शतानि च । उत्सृज्येह प्रयाता वै बान्धवा भृशदुःखिताः ॥५८॥
verses.english: Leaving here thousands of both friends and enemies, kinsmen stricken with grief go back to their homes.

verses.sanskrit: त्यज्यतामेष निस्तेजाः शून्यः काष्ठत्वमागतः । अन्यदेहविषक्तं हि शावं काष्ठत्वमागतम् ॥५९॥
verses.english: Leave off this dead body which has no longer any animal heat in it and which is as stiff as a piece of wood. Why then do you not go away, leaving the body of this child which is like a piece of wood and whose life had entered a new body?

verses.sanskrit: त्यक्तजीवस्य चैवास्य कस्माद्धित्वा न गच्छत । निरर्थको ह्ययं स्नेहो निष्फलश्च परिश्रमः ॥६०॥
चक्षुर्भ्यां न च कर्णाभ्यां संशृणोति समीक्षते । कस्मादेनं समुत्सृज्य न गृहान्गच्छताशु वै ॥६१॥
verses.english: This your love has no meaning, and this caressing of the child is useless. He does not see with his eyes or hear with ears.

verses.sanskrit: मोक्षधर्माश्रितैर्वाक्यैर्हेतुमद्भिः सुनिष्ठुरैः । मयोक्ता गच्छत क्षिप्रं स्वं स्वमेव निवेशनम् ॥६२॥
verses.english: Leaving him here go away forthwith. Thus addressed by me in words which are seemingly cruel but which in reality are reasonable and are directly connected with the great religion of emancipation, return he to your respective homes.

verses.sanskrit: प्रज्ञाविज्ञानयुक्तेन बुद्धिसंज्ञाप्रदायिना । वचनं श्राविता नूनं मानुषाः संन्यवर्तत । शोको द्विगुणतां याति दृष्ट्वा स्मृत्वा च चेष्टितम् ॥६३॥
verses.english: Addressed thus by the vulture gifted with wisdom and knowledge and capable of giving intelligence and awakening the understanding, those men were about to go away from the crematorium. Grief becomes two-fold two-fold on seeing its object and on remembering the acts of that object (in life).

verses.sanskrit: इत्येतद्वचनं श्रुत्वा सन्निवृत्तास्तु मानुषाः । अपश्यत्तं तदा सुप्तं द्रुतमागत्य जम्बुकः ॥६४॥
verses.english: Having heard these words of the vulture, the men resolved to leave that place. Just at that time the jackal, coming there quickly, spied the child lying in the sleep of death.

verses.sanskrit: जम्बुक उवाच । इमं कनकवर्णाभं भूषणैः समलंकृतम् । गृध्रवाक्यात् कथं पुत्रं त्यजध्वं पितृपिण्डदम् ॥६५॥
verses.english: Why, indeed, do you leave, at the vulture's suggestion, this child bearing golden hue, adorned with ornaments, and capable of giving the obsequial cake to his departed manes?

verses.sanskrit: न स्नेहस्य च विच्छेदो विलापरुदितस्य च । मृतस्यास्य परित्यागात् तापो वै भविता ध्रुवम् ॥६६॥
verses.english: If you abandon him, your love will not terminate, nor these piteous cries. On the other hand, your grief will multiply itself.

verses.sanskrit: श्रूयते शम्बुके शूद्रे हते ब्राह्मणदारकः । जीवितो धर्ममासाद्य रामात्सत्यपराक्रमात् ॥६७॥
verses.english: We have heard that a Shudra named Shambuka having been killed and virtue having been upheld by the powerful Rama, a (dead, Brahmana child was restored to life.

verses.sanskrit: तथा श्वेतस्य राजर्षेर्बालो दृष्टान्तमागतः । श्वेतेन धर्मनिष्ठेन मृतः संजीवितः पुनः ॥६८॥
verses.english: Likewise the son of the royal sage Shveta had died (prematurely). But the virtuous monarch succeeded in reviving his dead child.

verses.sanskrit: तथा कश्चिल्लभेत्सिद्धो मुनिर्वा देवतापि वा । कृपणानामनुक्रोशं कुर्याद्वो रुदतामिह ॥६९॥
verses.english: Similarly, in your case also, some sage or god may be willing to grant your desire and show mercy to you that are crying piteously.

verses.sanskrit: इत्युक्तास्ते न्यवर्तन्त शोकार्ताः पुत्रवत्सलाः । अङ्के शिरः समाधाय रुरुदुर्बहुविस्तरम् । तेषां रुदितशब्देन गृध्रोऽभ्येत्य वचोऽब्रवीत् ॥७०॥
verses.english: Thus accosted by the jackai, the men, stricken with grief and full of affection for the child, returned, and placing the child's head on their laps one after another, began the bewail piteously. Hearing their cries, the vulture, coming there, once more spoke to them as follows.

verses.sanskrit: गृध्र उवाच । अश्रुपातपरिक्लिन्नः पाणिस्पर्शप्रपीडितः । धर्मराजप्रयोगाच्च दीर्घनिद्रां प्रवेशितः ॥७१॥
verses.english: The Vulture said Why are you bathing this child with your tears? Why are you pressing him with your palms in this way? At the behest of the grim king of justice the child has been sent to that sleep which will never be broken.

verses.sanskrit: तपसापि हि संयुक्ता धनवन्तो महाधियः । सर्वे मृत्युवशं यान्ति तदिदं प्रेतपत्तनम् ॥७२॥
verses.english: Those who have acquired the merit of penances, those who are gifted with wealth, those who are endued with great intelligence, in fact, all yield to death. This is the place intended for the dead.

verses.sanskrit: बालवृद्धसहस्राणि सदा सन्त्यज्य बान्धवाः । दिनानि चैव रात्रीश्च दुःखं तिष्ठन्ति भूतले ॥७३॥
verses.english: It is always seen that casting off thousands of kinsmen, young and old kinsmen pass their nights and days in grief, rolling on the naked earth.

verses.sanskrit: अलं निर्बन्धमागत्य शोकस्य परिधारणे । अप्रत्ययं कुतो ह्यस्य पुनरद्येह जीवितम् ॥७४॥
verses.english: Stop this ardour in putting on the trappings of woe. It is impossible that this child would be restored to life again.

verses.sanskrit: मृतस्योत्सृष्टदेहस्य पुनर्देहो न विद्यते । नैव मूर्तिप्रदानेन जम्बुकस्य शतैरपि ॥७५॥
verses.english: He will not regain his life ai the call of the jackal. If a person once dies and deserts his body, this body never regains animation.

verses.sanskrit: शक्यं जीवयितुं ह्येष बालो वर्षशतैरपि । अथ रुद्रः कुमारो वा ब्रह्मा वा विष्णुरेव च ॥७६॥
verses.english: By sacrificing their own lives, hundreds of jackals will not be able to revive this child in hundreds of years.

verses.sanskrit: वरमस्मै प्रयच्छेयुस्ततो जीवेदयं शिशुः । नैव बाष्पविमोक्षेण न वा श्वासकृते न च ॥७७॥
verses.english: If, however, Rudra, Kumara, Brahma, or Vishnu, grant him a boon, then only may this child be restored to life.

verses.sanskrit: न दीर्घरुदितेनायं पुनर्जीवं गमिष्यति । अहं च क्रोष्टुकश्चैव यूयं ये चास्य बान्धवाः ॥७८॥
verses.english: Neither the shedding of tears, nor the heaving of long sighs, nor profuse lamentations, will restore this one to life.

verses.sanskrit: धर्माधर्मौ गृहीत्वेह सर्वे वर्तामहेऽध्वनि । अप्रियं परुषं चापि परद्रोहं परस्त्रियम् ॥७९॥
verses.english: Myself, the jackal, you all, and all the relatives of this one, with all our virtues and sins, are vending the same way. Seek with care virtue, truth, the good of others justice, mercy for all creature, sincerity and honesty. They incur sin who, while living, do not take care of their parents, kinsmen and friends.

verses.sanskrit: अधर्ममनृतं चैव दूरात्प्राज्ञो विवर्जयेत् । धर्मं सत्यं श्रुतं न्याय्यं महतीं प्राणिनां दयाम् ॥८०॥
अजिह्मत्वमशाठ्यं च यत्नतः परिमार्गत । मातरं पितरं वापि बान्धवान् सुहृदस्तथा ॥८१॥
जीवतो ये न पश्यन्ति तेषां धर्मविपर्ययः । यो न पश्यति चक्षुर्भ्यां नेङ्गते च कथञ्चन ॥८२॥
तस्य निष्ठावसानान्ते रुदन्तः किं करिष्यथ । इत्युक्तास्ते सुतं त्यक्त्वा भूमौ शोकपरिप्लुताः । दह्यमानाः सुतस्नेहात्प्रययुर्बान्धवा गृहम् ॥८३॥
verses.english: What will you profit by crying, for him after death, who does not see with his eyes and stir in the least.

verses.sanskrit: जम्बुक उवाच । दारुणो मर्त्यलोकोऽयं सर्वप्राणिविनाशनः । इष्टबन्धुवियोगश्च तथेहाल्पं च जीवितम् ॥८४॥
verses.english: The jackal said Alas, dreadful is this world of mortals! Here no creature can escape. Every creature's life is short. Beloved friends are always going.

verses.sanskrit: बह्वलीकमसत्यं चाप्यतिवादाप्रियंवदम् । इमं प्रेक्ष्य पुनर्भावं दुःखशोकविवर्धनम् ॥८५॥
verses.english: It is full of vanities and falsehoods, accusations and evil reports! Witnessing again this incident which increases pain and grief, I do not for a moment like this world of men.

verses.sanskrit: न मे मानुषलोकोऽयं मुहूर्तमपि रोचते । अहो धिग्गृध्रवाक्येन यथैवाबुद्धयस्तथा ॥८६॥
कथं गच्छत निःस्नेहाः सुतस्नेहं विसृज्य च । प्रदीप्ताः पुत्रशोकेन सन्निवर्तत मानुषाः ॥८७॥
verses.english: Alas, shame on you, you men, who thus return like foolish persons, on hearing the vulture's words, though you are burning with grief on account of the death of this child. You cruel men, how can you go away, renouncing parental affection upon hearing the words of a sinful vulture of impure soul.

verses.sanskrit: श्रुत्वा गृध्रस्य वचनं पापस्येहाकृतात्मनः । सुखस्यानन्तरं दुःखं दुःखस्यानन्तरं सुखम् ॥८८॥
सुखदुःखावृते लोके नेहास्त्येकमनन्तरम् । इमं क्षितितले त्यक्त्वा बालं रूपसमन्वितम् ॥८९॥
verses.english: Happiness is followed by misery, and misery by happiness. In this world which has both happiness and misery, none of these two exists without break. You little-witted men, where will go, casting off on the naked earth this beautiful child, this son who is a13 ornament of your family. Verily, I cannot conceive that this child endued with grace, youth and beauty is dead.

verses.sanskrit: कुलशोभाकरं मूढाः पुत्रं त्यक्त्वा क्व यास्यथ । रूप-यौवनसम्पन्नं द्योतमानमिव श्रिया ॥९०॥
जीवन्तमेव पश्यामि मनसा नात्र संशयः । विनाशो नास्य न हि वै सुखं प्राप्स्यथ मानुषाः ॥९१॥
verses.english: It is not proper that he should die. It seems that you are sure to gain happiness. You who are stricken with grief for the death of this child will, forsooth, have good luck to-day.

verses.sanskrit: पुत्रशोकाभितप्तानां मृतानामद्य वः क्षमम् । सुखसम्भावनं कृत्वा धारयित्वा सुखं स्वयम् । त्यक्त्वा गमिष्यथ क्वाद्य समुत्सृज्याल्पबुद्धिवत् ॥९२॥
verses.english: Anticipating inconvenience and pain and seeking your own comfort, where will you, like persons of little intelligence, go, leaving this darling.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              तथा धर्मविरोधेन प्रियमिथ्याभिधायिना । श्मशानवासिना नित्यं रात्रिं मृगयता नृप ॥९३॥
verses.english: Bhishma said Thus, O king, the kinsmen of the dead child, unable to settle what they should do, were, for fulfilling his own purpose, induced by that sinful jackal who uttered sweet falsehoods-that dweller of the crematorium who went there every night in search of food.

verses.sanskrit: ततो मध्यस्थतां नीता वचनैरमृतोपमैः । जम्बुकेन स्वकार्यार्थं बान्धवास्तस्य धिष्ठिताः ॥९४॥
गृध्र उवाच । अयं प्रेतसमाकीर्णो यक्षराक्षससेवितः । दारुणः काननोद्देशः कौशिकैरभिनादितः ॥९५॥
verses.english: Dreadful is that spot, this wilderness, which resounds with the screams of owls and is filled with spirits and Yakshas and Rakshasas.

verses.sanskrit: भीमः सुघोरश्च तथा नीलमेघसमप्रभः । अस्मिञ्छवं परित्यज्य प्रेतकार्याण्युपासत ॥९६॥
verses.english: It appears dreadful like a mass of blue clouds. Casting off the body, perform the funeral rites.

verses.sanskrit: भानुवत्प्रयात्यस्तं यावच्च विमला दिशः । तावदेनं परित्यज्य प्रेतकार्याण्युपासत ॥९७॥
verses.english: Throwing away the body, perform those rites before the sun sets and before the points of compass are covered with darkness.

verses.sanskrit: नदन्ति परुषं श्येनाः शिवाः क्रोशन्ति दारुणम् । मृगेन्द्राः प्रतिनन्दन्ति रविरस्तं च गच्छति ॥९८॥
verses.english: The hawks are uttering hideous cries. Jackals are howling hideously. Lions are roaring. The sun is setting.

verses.sanskrit: चिताधूमेन नीलेन संरज्यन्ते च पादपाः । श्मशाने च निराहाराः प्रतिनर्दन्ति देवताः ॥९९॥
verses.english: The trees on the crematorium are appearing dark for the blue smoke of the funeral pyres. Stricken with hunger the carnivorous animals are yelling in rage.

verses.sanskrit: सर्वे विकृतदेहाश्चाप्यस्मिन्देशे सुदारुणे । युष्मान्प्रधर्षयिष्यन्ति विकृता मांसभोजिनः ॥१००॥
verses.english: All those creatures of dreadful forms which live in this fearful place, all those grim-visaged animals that haunt this desert, will soon attack you.

verses.sanskrit: क्रूरश्चायं वनोद्देशो भयमद्य भविष्यति । त्यज्यतां काष्ठभूतोऽयं मृष्यतां जाम्बुकं वचः ॥१०१॥
verses.english: This forest is certainly dreadful. Danger will beset you. The child is like a dry wood. Indeed, if you listen to these false and useless words of the jackal against your own good sense, all of your will surely meet with death.

verses.sanskrit: यदि जम्बुकवाक्यानि निष्फलान्यनृतानि च । श्रोष्यथ भ्रष्टविज्ञानास्ततः सर्वे विनंक्ष्यथ ॥१०२॥
जम्बुक उवाच । स्थीयतां नेह भेतव्यं यावत्तपति भास्करः । तावदस्मिन् सुते स्नेहादनिर्वेदेन वर्तत ॥१०३॥
verses.english: Remain where you are. There is no fear even in this desert as long as the sun shines. Do you remain herc hopefully, moved by parental affection till the sun sets.

verses.sanskrit: स्वैरं रुदन्तो विश्रब्धाश्चिरं स्नेहेन पश्यत । स्थीयतां यावदादित्यः किं च क्रव्यादभाषितैः ॥१०४॥
verses.english: Without any fear, bewailing as you please, continue to look at this child with loving eyes. Though this forest is dreadful, no danger will overtake you. In sooth, this wilderness is quiet and peaceful. It is here that the Pitris by thousands departed from the world. Wait as long as the sun shines. Of what avail are this vulture's words to you?

verses.sanskrit: यदि गृध्रस्य वाक्यानि तीव्राणि रभसानि च । गृह्णीत मोहितात्मानः सुतो वो न भविष्यति ॥१०५॥
verses.english: If, being stupefied, you follow the cruel and harsh words of the vulture, then your child will never regain life.

verses.sanskrit:
भीष्म उवाच।
              गृध्रोऽस्तमित्याह गतो गतो नेति च जम्बुकः । मृतस्य तं परिजनमूचतुस्तौ क्षुधान्वितौ ॥१०६॥
verses.english: Bhishma said The vulture then said to those men, that the sun had set. The jackal said that it was not so. Both the vulture and the jackal fell hungry and thus addressed thc kinsmen of the dead child.

verses.sanskrit: स्वकार्यबद्धकक्षौ तौ राजन् गृध्रोऽथ जम्बुकः । क्षुत्पिपासापरिश्रान्तौ शास्त्रमालम्ब्य जल्पतः ॥१०७॥
verses.english: Both of them were deterinined upon accomplishing their respective purposes. Exhausted with hunger and thirst, they thus quarrelled, taking advantage of the scriptures.

verses.sanskrit: तयोर्विज्ञानविदुषोर्द्वयोर्मुगपतत्रिणोः । वाक्यैरमृतकल्पैस्तैः प्रतिष्ठन्ति व्रजन्ति च ॥१०८॥
verses.english: Moved by these words, sweet as ambrosia, of those two creatures, viz., the bird and the beast, both of whom had wisdom and knowledge, the kinsmen at one time desired to go away and at another to remain there.

verses.sanskrit: शोकदैन्यसमाविष्टा रुदन्तस्तस्थिरे तदा । स्वकार्यकुशलाभ्यां ते सम्भ्राम्यन्ते ह नैपुणात् ॥१०९॥
verses.english: At last, actuated by sorrow and depression, they waited there, bewailing piteously. They did not know that the beast and the bird, very clever in achieving their ends, had only stupefied them (by their words).

verses.sanskrit: तथा तयोर्विवदतोर्विज्ञानविदुषोर्द्वयोः । बान्धवानां स्थितानां चाप्युपातिष्ठत शङ्करः ॥११०॥
verses.english: While both the bird and the beast were thus disputing and while the kinsmen of the dead child sat listening to them, the great god Shankara, urged by his divine consort (Uma), arrived there with eyes bathed in tears of mercy.

verses.sanskrit: देव्या प्रणोदितो देवः कारुण्यार्द्रीकृतेक्षणः । ततस्तानाह मनुजान् वरदोऽस्मीति शङ्करः ॥१११॥
verses.english: Addressing the kinsmen of the dead child, the god said,-I am Shankara the granter of boons!-With hearts laden with grief, those men laid themselves low before the great god and said to him in reply,-Bereft of this our only child, all of us are on the brink of death. Be you pleased to grant us life by granting life to this our son.

verses.sanskrit: ते प्रत्यूचुरिदं वाक्यं दुःखिताः प्रणताः स्थिताः । एकपुत्रविहीनानां सर्वेषां जीवितार्थिनाम् ॥११२॥
पुत्रस्य नो जीवदानाज्जीवितं दातुमर्हसि । एवमुक्तः स भगवान् वारिपूर्णेन चक्षुषा ॥११३॥
जीवितं स्म कुमाराय प्रादाद्वर्षशतानि वै । तथा गोमायुगृध्राभ्यां प्राददत्क्षुद्विनाशनम् ॥११४॥
verses.english: Thus begged, the illustrious god, taking up some water in his hands, granted to that dead child life extending for a hundred years.

verses.sanskrit: वरं पिनाकी भगवान् सर्वभूतहिते रतः । ततः प्रणम्य ते देवं प्रायो हर्षसमन्विताः ॥११५॥
verses.english: Ever engaged in the behoof of all creatures, the illustrious holder of Pinaka granted a boon to both the jackal and the vulture for which their hunger was appeased.

verses.sanskrit: कृतकृत्याः सुखं हृष्टाः प्रातिष्ठन्त तदा विभो । अनिवेदेन दीर्घेण निश्चयेन ध्रुवेण च ॥११६॥
verses.english: Filled with joy and having gained great prosperity, the men bowed to the god. Gaining success, they then, O king, left that spot in great glee. Through continued hopefulness and firm determination and the grace of the great god, the fruits of one's acts are gained forthwith.

verses.sanskrit: देवदेवप्रसादाच्च क्षिप्रं फलमवाप्यते । पश्य दैवस्य संयोगं बान्धवानां च निश्चयम् ॥११७॥
कृपणानां तु रुदतां कृतमश्रुप्रमार्जनम् । पश्य चाल्पेन कालेन निश्चयान्वेषणेन च ॥११८॥
verses.english: Mark the combination of circumstances and the determination of those kinsmen. While crying with heavy hearts, their tears were wiped and dried up.

verses.sanskrit: प्रसादं शङ्करात्प्राप्य दुःखिताः सुखमाप्नुवन् । ते विस्मिताः प्रहृष्टाश्च पुत्रसंजीवनात् पुनः ॥११९॥
verses.english: See, how within only a short time, through their firmness of resolution, they gained the grace of Shankara, and their sorrows removed, they were made happy.

verses.sanskrit: बभूवुर्भरतश्रेष्ठ प्रसादाच्छङ्करस्य वै । ततस्ते त्वरिता राजंस्त्यक्त्वा शोकं शिशूद्भवम् ॥१२०॥
verses.english: Indeed, through Shankara's favour, O chief of the Bharatas, those sorrowing kinsmen were filled with wonder and joy at the restoration of their child to life.

verses.sanskrit: विविशुः पुत्रमादाय नगरं हृष्टमानसाः । एषा बुद्धिः समस्तानां चातुर्वर्ण्येन दर्शिता ॥१२१॥
verses.english: Then, O king, shaking off that grief caused by their child, those Brahmanas, filled with joy, quickly returned to their town; taking the restored child with them. Such a conduct has been laid down for all the four castes.

verses.sanskrit: धर्मार्थमोक्षसंयुक्तमितिहासमिमं शुभम् । श्रुत्वा मनुष्यः सततमिहामुत्र प्रमोदते ॥१२२॥
verses.english: By frequently listening to this auspicious story fraught with virtue, profit, and emancipation, a man acquires happiness both in this world and the next.'
